claims.text: Spark plasma sintering with machine-learning-optimized parameters can control reaction kinetics in an RHEA/Cu powder blend.
The proposed SPS process will suppress phase segregation between the RHEA and Cu.
The proposed process will produce a fine-scale, homogeneous composite microstructure.
The resulting RHEA/Cu composite will be suitable for nuclear reactor applications.
Refractory alloying elements have a large positive heat of mixing with Cu.
Conventional processing of an RHEA/Cu blend tends to cause phase separation.
SPS can rapidly densify and react the RHEA/Cu powder blend.
Machine learning can optimize the heating rate, pressure, and reaction time for this SPS process.
RHEAs are relevant to structural service at elevated or extreme temperatures.
Controlled SPS conditions can replicate large-scale processing environments while mimicking elevated-temperature and irradiation conditions in advanced reactors.
The proposed process will create a fine-scale, kinetically trapped RHEA/Cu interface.
A fine-scale, kinetically trapped interface will limit macroscopic phase separation.
Rapid localized heating and high-pressure densification reduce the time available for thermodynamically driven phase separation.
ML-driven optimization can tailor the sintering profile to confine diffusion and reaction rates at the RHEA/Cu interface.
The SPS-processed composite will have less phase segregation and a more uniform microstructure than a conventionally sintered composite.
Reduced segregation will improve mechanical strength, thermal stability, and irradiation resistance relative to conventional processing.
Conventional melting or slower sintering permits RHEA/Cu phase separation because of the positive heat of mixing.
Industrial scale-up may introduce variables that are not represented in laboratory-scale optimization.

contradictions.description: The conditions claim that the SPS setup replicates large-scale processing environments, whereas the boundary states that industrial scale-up may introduce variables not captured during laboratory optimization.
